name: CENTRAL OREGON SPINE AND SPORTS
address: 2115 NE WYATT COURT STE 101, BEND, OR 97701

fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Circular Driveway; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Open Lawn Area; Detached Structure; Perimeter Fencing; Access Drive
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Circular Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install reflective address numbers visible from the road at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property at night or in low visibility.
• Mark the secondary access drive entrance with reflective posts or markers so responders can identify it quickly under stress or in the dark.
• Trim dense vegetation along the edges of the access drive to maintain clear vehicle width for fire apparatus and ambulances.
• Cut back vegetation that overhangs the access drive to maintain vertical clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Thin dense plantings near the detached structure so responders can move around it on foot without obstruction.
• Remove or cut back vegetation growing directly against the main residence and detached structure to allow responders to work along exterior walls.
• Keep the circular driveway clear of parked vehicles so apparatus can complete a full loop without having to back out.
• Post clear signage or use pavement markings at the circular driveway entry point to direct responding units toward the correct flow of travel.
• Keep the rear access point unlocked and clearly marked so responders are not delayed finding or forcing entry to the rear of the property.
• Trim shrubs or trees along the perimeter fencing that block visibility of gate locations from the driveway or access drive.
• Identify a flat, stable staging area near the circular driveway and keep it free of vehicles, equipment, and landscaping

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Tree Cluster; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Open Green Space; Ground Vegetation; Scattered Trees; Multiple Access Routes
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters nearest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove or trim shrubs growing close to the structure's exterior walls.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so individual trees are not touching or overlapping each other.
• Clear ground vegetation growing directly against the base of the structure.
• Keep tree branches trimmed so they do not hang over or touch the roof or walls.
• Thin the densest tree clusters on the property to reduce the amount of connected vegetation between trees.
• Maintain the open green space areas by keeping them mowed short and free of dead plant material.
• Keep scattered shrubs spread across the property trimmed low and separated from nearby trees and structures.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so emergency vehicles can move freely.
• Maintain clear sightlines around the structure by trimming or removing vegetation that blocks views from multiple sides.
